findings.message: `this.state` is written to directly. React does not see the write, so nothing re-renders, and the next `setState` merges into the state object React still believes is current and silently discards what was written here. The bug surfaces later and somewhere else, as a value that was set and then was not. Call `setState` with the new value instead, and treat `this.state` as read-only everywhere but the constructor.

clean.source: var H = createClass({ m: function() { this.state.x = 1; } });
